ctx.x: We will go now to where I am at Austin High School and I don't have an instrument yet, but the McPartland brothers talked to my father -- talked my father into buying me a C-Melody saxophone, which he bought at -- I think I was 16; yes -- the age of 16 and two years later, I played my first professional job with no study at all on the C-Melody and that was at a place called the Sheboygan Inn in Sheboygan, Wisconsin. It was right on the lake.

Now, there was a pianist by the name of Lyman Woods, who had a trio -- that is, he wanted a trio and he loved Dave Tough -- Dave Tough was his favorite drummer and he wanted an alto saxophone player, or a tenor, anything, a good saxophone player. Dave Tough told him that I was the best C-Melody saxophone player around and actually, I could hardly play. I couldn't play melody. I could play a few notes.
They always said I had a good beat. Well, that one beat and one note came out in everything I played.
